title: Tenant-side aggregator for on-prem flow control and metadata enrichment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight tenant-side aggregator daemon for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that performs per-tenant flow-control, identity enforcement, metadata enrichment, sampling, and redaction before forwarding traces/logs/metrics to Redwood ingest or a local sink. The goal is to provide robust tenant isolation and predictable observability behavior in constrained or air-gapped environments while keeping the aggregator small, auditable, and easy to deploy as an init container, sidecar, or host process.
background: Current on-prem collectors sometimes forward noisy telemetry that violates tenant isolation goals (PII leakage, cross-tenant sampling differences) and create bursty load that destabilizes perimeter gateways. Existing tickets addressed gateway sharding and collector isolation (see ENG-4721 and ENG-20456) but we lack a composable tenant-side component that enforces policy closer to the source and provides stable shaping/backpressure for Dedicated pools and private clusters.
proposal:
Implement a modular tenant-side aggregator with the following core capabilities:
- Auth & identity: mTLS + SPIFFE or onboarding token verification; attach tenant_id to every envelope.
- Per-tenant flow-control: token-bucket rate-limiting and cooperative backpressure to avoid overwhelming perimeter forwarders.
- Metadata enrichment: append runtime tags (cluster, node, deployment, model-version) and rollout flags required for per-route dashboards and SLO attribution.
- Sampling & dynamic filters: configurable head-based sampling with per-tenant policies and adaptive sampling that can be tuned from Console.
- Redaction & schema validation: apply tenant-specific redaction rules and structured-output validation to prevent PII leaks.
- Deterministic trace-id translation: preserve single global trace context while rewriting trace IDs to a tenant-scoped namespace to prevent accidental cross-tenant correlation in multi-tenant ingest.
- Sink multiplexing: local buffering to disk, forward to Redwood ingest endpoint, or send to customer-backed sinks depending on network availability and policy.
- Lightweight admin API for health, backpressure metrics, and runtime config via file or metadata service for air-gapped setups.
tradeoffs: We keep the aggregator intentionally opinionated and small to minimize security surface and maintenance burden; more advanced processing (heavy enrichment, ML-powered sampling) remains in upstream pipelines. Running enrichment on the host increases CPU usage on customer nodes vs. doing everything at perimeter; we mitigate by providing strict resource guidance and offering a stripped-down minimal mode for constrained hosts. Deterministic trace-id translation reduces risk of cross-tenant analytics but requires mapping tables for trace lookups in support flows.
decisions: Use Go for the aggregator binary to keep a small, single-binary footprint and simple dependency story
Expose config via file + env with optional dynamic config hook for Console-initiated policy updates
Default to permissive local sink + occasional push to Redwood ingest to support intermittent connectivity in air-gapped installs
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator builds into single statically-linked binary and passes CI linting
Per-tenant rate-limiting prevents >95% of tenant bursts from increasing egress rates to the perimeter gateway during load tests
Trace id translation demonstrated: same incoming trace becomes tenant-scoped trace with lookup mapping available to SRE tools
Redaction rules applied in test corpus with zero PII leakage as verified by unit+fuzz tests
Admin endpoints expose per-tenant metrics (ingest rate, dropped, buffered, sample rate) and are scrapeable by Prometheus
Deployment manifests (DaemonSet, sidecar & init container examples) included in repo and verified in QA cluster
Works offline: in air-gapped mode, data persists to disk and forwarder resumes delivery when network restored
tasks: Prototype aggregator: auth, tenant-id attach, basic rate-limiter
Implement deterministic trace-id translation and unit tests
Integrate redaction engine and sampling policies
Implement disk-backed buffer and sink multiplexing
Add admin metrics and health endpoints
Write deployment manifests (DaemonSet, sidecar, host process) and example kustomize overlays
Docs: operator runbook, config reference, Console integration guide
Ship alpha to Dedicated customers and two Private beta customers

testing_plan: Run distributed load tests that simulate 100 tenants with skewed traffic (10% tenants generate 80% of events). Verify backpressure prevents gateway egress spikes and measure P50/P95 processing latency; unit + integration tests for redaction and trace-id translation, plus chaos test where forwarder drops network for 30 minutes to validate disk-buffer durability.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood in staging 2) Alpha release to Dedicated infra team 3) Two Private customer pilots (explicit opt-in) with SLA guardrails 4) Gradual ramp to all Dedicated clusters with Console config defaults and migration docs. Provide rollback runbooks and toggle for disabling enrichment if unexpected regressions occur.
